title: Palimpsest Tasklet Curation + Observability Gateway for Support Automation
creator: Michael Chen
description:
Summary: Curate a lightweight catalog of idempotent 'tasklets' (small, composable procedural recipes) that can be executed by support oncall or automatically by the admin automation pipeline. Build an Observability Gateway that anchors telemetry snapshots (prefix traces, token-level cost estimates, KV cache deltas) to each tasklet execution so we can audit, dry-run, and compare regressions across runtime and model variants.

Background: We have a proliferation of long runbooks and monolithic scripts that are hard for SREs and oncall engineers to safely run. This project breaks procedures into typed tasklets with enforced inputs, dry-run capability, and telemetry anchors. The palimpsest model: every tasklet execution produces an immutable execution record layered over prior runs (like a palimpsest) so we can revert, replay, and diff behavior.

Goals: Create a tasklet schema, authoring UI hooks for Console, a light runtime for safe execution (idempotency + permission checks), and an Observability Gateway that captures and stores telemetry snapshots for each run. Provide APIs for: list/search tasklets, execute(dry-run|live), attach/verify inputs, and fetch execution snapshots.

Non-goals: This ticket does not replace the full runbook repo or convert all legacy scripts; conversion will be incremental and handled via migration tasks. Not targeting multi-region Dedicated routing in this scope.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- Schema vs. flexibility: we enforce a minimal typed input/outputs schema to avoid freeform scripts; this costs some author friction but reduces incidents.
- Where to store telemetry snapshots: opted for S3-backed snapshot store with a small index in Postgres (existing telemetry pipeline already integrates with this pattern) instead of writing to primary runtime DB to reduce blast radius.
- Dry-run fidelity: dry-run will simulate API calls where safe (read-only checks) and record intended side-effects in the snapshot rather than execute external side-effectful operations. We accepted some false negatives to avoid hitting production systems.

Implementation approach:
1) Tasklet schema and linter (YAML/JSON): inputs, outputs, required_permissions, idempotency_token, timeout_ms.
2) Tasklet runtime shim: small service that validates inputs, performs a permission check against RBAC, executes preflight dry-run, then executes live if requested.
3) Observability Gateway: intercepts tasklet runtime events, records token-cost estimate, KV cache deltas, model variant, runtime kernel profile, and stores snapshot with an execution-id.
4) Console integration: authoring flow adds a 'Publish as tasklet' button and a preview dry-run pane.
5) Migration helper script to convert highest-frequency runbooks to tasklets for a pilot.
acceptance_criteria: Schema and linter merged in monorepo (pass on CI).
Runtime shim deployed to staging and able to run dry-run against three pilot tasklets.
Observability Gateway records snapshots with execution-id and exposes a stable URL for Console to fetch.
Console shows dry-run preview, permission gating, and a publish flow for tasklet authors.
Two high-frequency oncall runbooks converted to tasklets and validated by support team in staging.
End-to-end telemetry shows cost estimate + KV cache delta for live executions in the snapshot view.
migration_notes: Start with runbooks that have <=5 steps and <3 external writes.
Use conversion script to split monolithic scripts into 1..N tasklets and annotate idempotency tokens.
risk_mitigation: RBAC enforced at runtime; only members of support-runbooks group can publish in prod.
All live executions require a canary flag for first two weeks post-release.
Snapshots are scrubbed for PII via existing telemetry scrubber before storage.
